title: Crush Your Enemy Totally
summary: This law stresses acting pragmatically during conflict by completely eliminating your opponents. Showing mercy out of pity or guilt often backfires because defeated enemies feel humiliated and obligated, driving them to seek revenge as soon as the tide turns. To ensure absolute security, one must crush both the enemy's physical power and their spirit to fight back, leaving no opportunity for a comeback.
example: Two rival generals where one repeatedly spared his old friend out of sentimentality, enabling the smart general to escape and eventually execute him when power shifted.
Lady Wu, who exercised absolute ruthlessness—even against her own children—to eliminate any threats to her rule and retain power.
reversal: Refraining from direct action if an enemy will be destroyed by their own mistakes or by a third party, avoiding unnecessary risk.
Offering mercy only when the opponent is completely depowered with zero possibility of a comeback, provided you never lower your guard.
